summary: The note argues that the rise of e-commerce is reshaping retail employment, not eliminating it. Retail roles are shifting from in-store sales toward digital, logistics, and tech-oriented jobs, so workers and small retailers must reskill and build an online presence. Governments, educators, and employers are urged to support the transition through training programs.
one_line: E-commerce growth is transforming retail jobs toward digital skills, making reskilling, online presence, and training programs essential for workers and retailers.
key_facts: A Global E-commerce Association study published September 15, 2023 reported online sales growing 35% year over year since 2021.
Amazon and Walmart added 20,000 new jobs in the last quarter, as reported by market analyst Jane Doe on October 1, 2023.
Eden & Avery announced on September 22, 2023 that it would retrain 15,000 employees to manage online sales, social media interactions, and supply chain logistics.
Retail consultant Michael Thompson said, "The future belongs to those who adapt."
New job categories include social media coordinators, online customer service representatives, digital merchandisers, and 'retail technologists' who oversee AI-driven retail environments.
Warehouse robotics and automated inventory systems are replacing jobs once held by stock handlers and inventory clerks.

John Parker, owner of the local bookstore 'Page Turners,' revamped his website, used social media marketing, and hosts virtual book club meetings, and has hired more web developers and online community managers.
Parker made his remarks on November 3, 2023, explaining that the changes followed decreased foot traffic.
Jane Doe said "Ecommerce is not just a sales channel but a means of survival."
On September 30, 2023, Doe reported that traditional retailers who bolstered their online presence saw a 10-15% increase in sales versus those who did not.
The Retail Workforce Digital Uplift program, launched on October 20, 2023, aims to fast-track the digital education of current retail workers.
The note says e-commerce has seen meteoric adoption growth since the onset of the global pandemic in early 2020.
The note frames e-commerce as an opportunity rather than a threat, requiring a blend of traditional customer service skills and digital acumen.
